Attic band spans the low raised attic between corner shoulders; full-width cornice stays below it. Its previous full-width placement exceeded the admitted end-shoulder silhouette and is retained as failed attempt5.

Portal sandstone field and projecting entablature use shared aperture-cut masonry bands/blocks. Rusticated joint grooves, curved scrollwork and fine carving remain unresolved. Corner quoin width revised from .035 to .055 frontage fraction after current photo/independent review; course positions remain coarse source-informed drawing inputs, not exact stone measurements.

Source-visible horizontal landing rail connects the upper flight posts using the shared rail-only assembly; dimensions remain the same bounded drawing clearance/depth as the adjoining rails. No new stairs or hidden tread count are inferred.

Cornice groups use source-visible broad consoles, short lip pendants and three historical lower triglyph fragments from herengracht-433-frieze-observation.json. Current foliage and blur obscure parts of the left and lower-right frieze; no mirrored right triglyph count is inferred. Three grooves and section depths are coarse reusable drawing patterns, not exact measurements of carving.

Continuous shallow stone backing retained behind the projecting cornice lip and pendants; gaps between discrete ornaments are not holes into brown masonry. Triglyph shoulders use shallow beveled original geometry to expose relief in flat-color daylight.
